facts.title: The Armenian carpet
facts.text: Weaving tools dating to the 3rd and 2nd millennia BC have been unearthed at Teghut and Shengavit.

facts.title: The Pazyryk carpet
facts.text: The oldest pile-knotted carpet to survive intact, made with the Armenian double knot, dyed with Armenian cochineal.

facts.title: Dragon carpets
facts.text: The vishapagorg combine the stylized dragon with the tree of life, the phoenix and crenellated geometric forms.

facts.title: A name from Karin
facts.text: Kali or khali, the word for knotted carpets throughout the Muslim world, derives from the Armenian city of Karin.

facts.title: "The finest in the world"
facts.text: That is how Marco Polo described the pieces made by Armenian artisans.

facts.title: Four million knots
facts.text: In Ghazir, four hundred orphan girls crafted a rug of the Garden of Eden, later presented to the White House.

facts.title: Very much alive
facts.text: Artsakh Carpet was founded in 2013 in Stepanakert, the same year a carpet museum opened its doors in Shushi.

ytTitle: The Armenian carpet, a millenary heritage woven with history
ytLead: From weaving tools of the 3rd and 2nd millennia BC to today's workshops, discover the art of the Armenian carpet, a textile treasure of symbols, craftsmanship and history.
